content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship Him.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Præcursóris Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship Him.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Psalmus 1 [1]
content.english: Psalm 1 [1]

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
content.english: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

content.english: Psalm 2 [2]

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
content.english: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

content.latin: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
content.english: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

content.latin: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
content.english: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

content.latin: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
content.english: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

content.latin: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

content.latin: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
content.english: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

content.latin: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
content.english: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

content.latin: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
content.english: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Incipit liber Ieremíæ Prophétæ
content.english: Lesson from the book of Jeremias

content.latin: 1 Verba Ieremíæ fílii Helcíæ, de sacerdótibus, qui fuérunt in Anathoth, in terra Béniamin.
content.english: 1 The words of Jeremias the son of Helcias, of the priests that were in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin.

content.latin: 2 Quod factum est verbum Dómini ad eum in diébus Iosíæ fílii Amon regis Iuda, in tertiodécimo anno regni eius.
content.english: 2 The word of the Lord which came to him in the days of Josias the son of Amon king of Juda, in the thirteenth year of his reign.

content.latin: 3 Et factum est in diébus Ióakim fílii Iosíæ regis Iuda, usque ad consummatiónem undécimi anni Sedecíæ fílii Iosíæ regis Iuda, usque ad transmigratiónem Ierúsalem, in mense quinto.
content.english: 3 And which came to him in the days of Joakim the son of Josias king of Juda, unto the end of the eleventh year of Sedecias the son of Josias king of Juda, even unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive, in the fifth month.

content.latin: 4 Et factum est verbum Dómini ad me, dicens:
content.english: 4 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

content.latin: 5 Priúsquam te formárem in útero, novi te: et ántequam exíres de vulva, sanctificávi te, et prophétam in géntibus dedi te.
content.english: 5 Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee: and before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee, and made thee a prophet unto the nations.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Ioánnes:
content.english: ℟. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.

content.latin: * Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine, et paráret Dómino plebem perféctam.
content.english: * The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Erat Ioánnes in desérto prǽdicans baptísmum pœniténtiæ.
content.english: ℣. John was in the wilderness, preaching the baptism of repentance.

content.latin: ℟. Hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine, et paráret Dómino plebem perféctam.
content.english: ℟. The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 6 Et dixi, A a a, Dómine Deus: ecce néscio loqui, quia puer ego sum.
content.english: 6 And I said: Ah, ah, ah, Lord God: behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child.

content.latin: 7 Et dixit Dóminus ad me: Noli dícere, Puer sum: quóniam ad ómnia, quæ mittam te, ibis: et univérsa, quæcúmque mandávero tibi, loquéris.
content.english: 7 And the Lord said to me: Say not: I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee: and whatsoever I shall command thee, thou shalt speak.

content.latin: 8 Ne tímeas a fácie eórum: quia tecum ego sum, ut éruam te, dicit Dóminus.
content.english: 8 Be not afraid at their presence: for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the Lord.

content.latin: 9 Et misit Dóminus manum suam, et tétigit os meum: et dixit Dóminus ad me: Ecce dedi verba mea in ore tuo:
content.english: 9 And the Lord put forth his hand, and touched my mouth: and the Lord said to me: Behold I have given my words in thy mouth:

content.latin: 10 Ecce constítui te hódie super gentes, et super regna, ut evéllas, et déstruas, et dispérdas, et díssipes, et ædífices, et plantes.
content.english: 10 Lo, I have set thee this day over the nations, and over the kingdoms, to root up, and pull down, and to waste, and to destroy, and to build, and to plant.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Elísabeth Zacharíæ magnum virum génuit, Ioánnem Baptístam, præcursórem Dómini:
content.english: ℟. Elizabeth, the wife of Zacharias, was the mother of a mighty man, even of John the Baptist, the Forerunner of the Lord,

content.latin: * Qui viam Dómino præparávit in erémo.
content.english: * who made straight in the desert an highway for the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Ioánnes.
content.english: ℣. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.

content.latin: ℟. Qui viam Dómino præparávit in erémo.
content.english: ℟. Who made straight in the desert an highway for the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 17 Tu ergo accínge lumbos tuos, et surge, et lóquere ad eos ómnia quæ ego præcípio tibi. Ne formídes a fácie eórum: nec enim timére te fáciam vultum eórum.

content.latin: Sermo 20 de Sanctis
content.english: 20th on the Saints.

content.latin: Post illum sacrosánctum Dómini natális diem, nullíus hóminum nativitátem légimus celebrári, nisi solíus beáti Ioánnis Baptístæ. In áliis Sanctis et eléctis Dei nóvimus illum diem coli, quo illos, post consummatiónem labórum et devíctum triumphatúmque mundum, in perpétuas æternitátes præsens hæc vita partúriit. In áliis consummáta últimi diéi mérita celebrántur: in hoc étiam prima dies, et ipsa étiam hóminis inítia consecrántur; pro hac absque dúbio causa, quia per hunc Dóminus advéntum suum, ne súbito hómines insperátum non agnóscerent, vóluit esse testátum. Ioánnes autem figúra fuit véteris Testaménti, et in se formam prǽtulit legis; et ídeo Ioánnes prænuntiávit Salvatórem, sicut lex grátiam præcucúrrit.
content.english: Outside the most holy Birthday of the Lord, we find celebrated in the Gospel the birth of only one other, namely, that of the blessed Baptist, John. As regardeth all others among God's holy and chosen ones we know that that day is observed whereon, with their work finished, and the world conquered and finally trampled down, they were born from this into a better life, even one of everlasting blessedness. In others is honoured the crowning of the struggle on their last day of dying life, but in John is honoured the first day; in him the very beginning is found hallowed. And the reason of this is, without doubt, because he was sent from God to bear witness to the coming of the Light, lest when It came It might take the darkness by surprise, and the darkness might not comprehend It. Now, John was a figure of the Old Testament, and showed in his own person a typical embodiment of the Law; and therefore John heralded beforehand the coming of the Saviour, even as the Law was our schoolmaster to bring us to the grace of Christ. Gal. iii. 24.

content.latin: Quod autem nondum natus de secréto matérni úteri prophetávit, et expers lucis iam testis est veritátis; hoc est intellegéndum, quod latens sub velámine et carne lítteræ, et Redemptórem mundo spíritu prædicávit, et nobis Dóminum nostrum de quodam legis útero proclamávit. Ergo quia Iudǽi erravérunt a ventre, id est, a lege quæ a Christo grávida erat, erravérunt a ventre, locúti sunt falsa; ídeo hic venit in testimónium, ut testimónium perhibéret de lúmine.
content.english: But as touching this, that he prophesied while yet in the hidden depths of his mother's womb, and while himself lightless bore testimony to the truth, we are to understand it as a figure how that while himself wrapped round with the veil and carnal ordinances of the letter, he by the spirit preached unto the world a Redeemer, and testified that Jesus is our Lord even while for himself, working under the law, the birth of the new dispensation was still in the womb of the future, and not come to day. The Jews were estranged from the womb, that is from the Law, that womb heavy with the Christ That was to be; they went astray from the belly, speaking lies, Ps. lvii. 4; and therefore John came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe. John i. 7.

content.english: * For even this is John, who made straight in the desert an highway for our God. This also is he which bare witness, saying: Behold the Lamb of God! And his light lightened the minds of men.

content.latin: Quod autem Ioánnes in cárcere constitútus ad Christum discípulos suos órdinat; lex ad Evangélium transmíttit. Quæ lex iuxta typum Ioánnis, quasi ignorántiæ clausa cárcere, in obscúro et in occúlto iacébat, et Iudáica cæcitáte sensus intra lítteram tenebátur inclúsus. De hoc beátus Evangelísta prolóquitur: Ille erat lucérna ardens, id est, Spíritus Sancti igne succénsus, ut mundo ignorántiæ nocte possésso lumen salútis osténderet, et quasi inter densíssimas delictórum ténebras splendidíssimus iustítiæ solem lucis suæ rádio demonstráret, et de seípso dicens: Ego vox clamántis in desérto.
content.english: But as for this, that when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples Matth. xi. 2; this is the Law sending to the Gospel. For John here was a figure of the Law, imprisoned in ignorance, lying in the dark, and in a hidden place, and he was fettered through Jewish misunderstanding within the bonds of the letter. But of him was it said, as is written in the Blessed Evangelist He was a burning and a shining light that is to say, that, when the whole world was wrapt in the night of ignorance, this Saint was kindled by the fire of the Holy Ghost, to show before men the light of salvation, and at the hour of the thickest darkness of sin, appeared like a bright morning star to herald the rising of that Sun so right gloriously radiant, the Son of righteousness, Christ our Lord. And this is why John said of himself: I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord. John i. 15.

content.english: 20:12 For they have intended evils against thee: * they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.

content.english: 33:4 O magnify the Lord with me; * and let us extol his name together.

content.english: 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me; * and he delivered me from all my troubles.

content.english: 33:6 Come ye to him and be enlightened: * and your faces shall not be confounded.

content.english: 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: * and saved him out of all his troubles.

content.english: 33:8 The Angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: * and shall deliver them.

content.english: 33:9 O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: * blessed is the man that hopeth in him.

content.latin: 33:10 Timéte Dóminum, omnes sancti eius: * quóniam non est inópia timéntibus eum.
content.english: 33:10 Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: * for there is no want to them that fear him.

content.latin: 33:11 Dívites eguérunt et esuriérunt: * inquiréntes autem Dóminum non minuéntur omni bono.
content.english: 33:11 The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: * but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.

content.latin: 33:12 Veníte, fílii, audíte me: * timórem Dómini docébo vos.
content.english: 33:12 Come, children, hearken to me: * I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

content.latin: 33:13 Quis est homo qui vult vitam: * díligit dies vidére bonos?
content.english: 33:13 Who is the man that desireth life: * who loveth to see good days?

content.latin: 33:14 Próhibe linguam tuam a malo: * et lábia tua ne loquántur dolum.
content.english: 33:14 Keep thy tongue from evil, * and thy lips from speaking guile.

content.latin: 33:15 Divérte a malo, et fac bonum: * inquíre pacem, et perséquere eam.
content.english: 33:15 Turn away from evil and do good: * seek after peace and pursue it.

content.latin: 33:16 Óculi Dómini super iustos: * et aures eius in preces eórum.
content.english: 33:16 The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: * and his ears unto their prayers.

content.latin: 33:17 Vultus autem Dómini super faciéntes mala: * ut perdat de terra memóriam eórum.
content.english: 33:17 But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: * to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.

content.english: 33:18 The just cried, and the Lord heard them: * and delivered them out of all their troubles.

content.english: 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the just; * but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.

content.latin: 33:21 Custódit Dóminus ómnia ossa eórum: * unum ex his non conterétur.
content.english: 33:21 The Lord keepeth all their bones, * not one of them shall be broken.

content.latin: 33:22 Mors peccatórum péssima: * et qui odérunt iustum, delínquent.
content.english: 33:22 The death of the wicked is very evil: * and they that hate the just shall be guilty.

content.latin: 33:23 Rédimet Dóminus ánimas servórum suórum: * et non delínquent omnes qui sperant in eo.
content.english: 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: * and none of them that trust in him shall offend.

content.latin: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
content.english: From the Holy Gospel according to Luke

content.latin: Elísabeth implétum est tempus pariéndi, et péperit fílium. Et audiérunt vicíni et cognáti eius quia magnificávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam cum illa, et congratulabántur ei. Et réliqua.
content.english: Elisabeth's fullness of time came that she should deliver, and she brought forth a son. And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had showed great mercy upon her, and they rejoiced with her. And so on.

content.latin: Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
content.english: Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop of Milan.

content.latin: Liber 2 Comm. in Lucæ cap. 1, ante finem
content.english: Bk. ii. Comm. on Luke i.

content.latin: Péperit fílium Elísabeth, et congratulabántur vicíni. Habet Sanctórum edítio lætítiam plurimórum, quia commúne est bonum; iustítia enim commúnis est virtus. Et ídeo in ortu iusti futúræ vitæ insígne præmíttitur, et grátia secutúræ virtútis exsultatióne vicinórum præfiguránte signátur. Pulchre autem tempus, quo fuit in útero Prophéta, descríbitur, ne Maríæ præséntia taceátur; sed tempus silétur infántiæ, eo quia infántiæ impediménta nescívit. Et ídeo in Evangélio nihil super eo légimus, nisi ortum eius, et oráculum, exsultatiónem in útero, vocem in desérto.
content.english: Elizabeth's full time came that she should be delivered, and she brought forth a son. And her neighbours rejoiced with her. The birth of a Saint is a joy for many, for it is a good to all. Righteousness is an help to all, and therefore when a righteous man is born it is an heralding of his life, which is still to come, that the helpful excellency of his future should be hailed by the, as it were, prophetic joy of the neighbours. It is well that we should be told concerning the prophet, while he was yet in the womb, that we may know how that Mary was there; but we hear nothing of his childhood, because, we know that it was safe and strong through the nearness of the Lord, Himself then in that womb which was free from the sorrows of pregnancy. And therefore we read in the Gospel nothing touching him save his coming, the annunciation thereof to his father, the leap which he gave in the womb, and his crying in the wilderness.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Præcúrsor Dómini venit, de quo ipse testátur:
content.english: ℟. The Fore-runner of the Lord cometh, to whom He Himself bare witness, saying:

content.latin: * Nullus maior inter natos mulíerum Ioánne Baptísta.
content.english: * Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.

content.latin: ℣. Hic est enim prophéta, et plus quam prophéta, de quo Salvátor ait.
content.english: ℣. A Prophet? Yea, and much more than a Prophet. This is he of whom the Saviour saith:

content.latin: ℟. Nullus maior inter natos mulíerum Ioánne Baptísta.
content.english: ℟. Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. He whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocate with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Neque enim ullam infántiæ sensit ætátem, qui supra natúram, supra ætátem in útero pósitus matris, a mensúra cœpit ætátis plenitúdinis Christi. Mire sanctus Evangelísta præmitténdum putávit, quod plúrimi infántem patris nómine Zacharíam appellándum putáverint; ut advértas matri non nomen alicúius displicuísse degéneris, sed id Sancto infúsum Spíritu, quod ab Angelo ante Zacharíæ fúerat prænuntiátum. Et quidem ille mutus intimáre vocábulum fílii nequívit uxóri; sed per prophetíam Elísabeth dídicit, quod non didícerat a maríto.
content.english: It was not for him to feel childishness, who beyond all use of nature or of his age, when as yet he lay in his mother's womb, leapt at once unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ. Eph. iv. 13. It is strange how that the Holy Evangelist hath judged meet to tell us that they thought to call the child Zacharias, after the name of his father, that thou mayest notice that the mother would have none of the names whereby their kindred were called, but only that name which the Holy Ghost had dictated, and which the Angel had told before unto Zacharias. The dumb man had certainly not been able to tell his wife by what name to call the child, and Elizabeth must needs have learnt by revelation what she could not have heard from her husband.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Gábriel Angelus appáruit Zacharíæ dicens: Nascétur tibi fílius, nomen eius Ioánnes vocábitur:
content.english: ℟. The Angel Gabriel appeared unto Zacharias, and said thy wife Elizabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John;

content.latin: * Et multi in nativitáte eius gaudébunt.
content.english: * And many shall rejoice at his birth.

content.latin: ℣. Erit enim magnus coram Dómino, vinum et síceram non bibet.
content.english: ℣. For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink.

content.latin: ℟. Et multi in nativitáte eius gaudébunt.
content.english: ℟. And many shall rejoice at his birth.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: ℟. And many shall rejoice at his birth.

content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ad societátem cívium supernórum perdúcat nos Rex Angelórum.
content.english: Benediction. May He that is the Angels' King to that high realm His people bring.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: Ioánnes est, inquit, nomen eius; hoc est, non nos ei nomen impónimus, qui iam a Deo nomen accépit. Habet vocábulum suum, quod agnóvimus, non quod elégimus. Habent hoc mérita Sanctórum, ut a Deo nomen accípiant. Sic Iacob Israël dícitur, quia Deum vidit. Sic Dóminus noster Iesus nominátus est, ántequam natus; cui non Angelus, sed Pater nomen impósuit. Vides Angelos quæ audíerint, non quæ usurpáverint, nuntiáre. Nec miréris, si nomen múlier, quod non audívit, asséruit; quando Spíritus ei Sanctus, qui Angelo mandáverat, revelávit.
content.english: His name is John; that is, it is not for us to choose a name now for him to whom God hath given a name already. He hath a name, which we know, but it is not one of our choosing. To receive a name from God is one of the honours of the Saints. Thus was it that Jacob's name was no more called Jacob but Israel, because he saw God face to face. Gen. xxxii. 28. Thus was it that our Lord Jesus was named before He was born, with a name not given by an Angel, but by the Father. Thou seest that Angels tell that which they have been bidden to tell, not matters of their own choosing. Nor oughtest thou to wonder that Elizabeth named a name which she had not heard, since it had been revealed to her by the same Holy Ghost Who had commanded the Angel to tell it.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: Te Deum

content.latin: Te Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
content.english: We praise thee, O God, * we acknowledge thee to be the Lord.

content.latin: Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
content.english: All the earth doth worship thee, * the Father everlasting.

content.latin: Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
content.english: To thee all Angels cry aloud, * the Heavens, and all the Powers therein.

content.latin: Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
content.english: To thee Cherubim and Seraphim * continually do cry.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
content.english: bow head Holy, Holy, Holy * Lord God of Sabaoth;

content.latin: Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: Heaven and earth are full * of the Majesty of thy glory.

content.latin: Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
content.english: The glorious company of the Apostles * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
content.english: The goodly fellowship of the Prophets * praise thee.

content.latin: Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
content.english: The noble army of Martyrs * praise thee.

content.latin: Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
content.english: The holy Church throughout all the world * doth acknowledge thee;

content.latin: Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
content.english: The Father, * of an infinite Majesty.

content.latin: Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
content.english: Thine honourable, true, * and only Son;

content.latin: Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
content.english: Also the Holy Ghost, * the Comforter.

content.latin: Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
content.english: Thou art the King of Glory, * O Christ.

content.latin: Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
content.english: Thou art the everlasting * Son of the Father.

content.latin: Fit reverentia Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
content.english: During the following verse all make a profound bow: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.

content.latin: Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
content.english: When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

content.latin: Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
content.english: Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.

content.latin: Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
content.english: We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.

content.latin: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui præséntem diem honorábilem nobis in beáti Ioánnis nativitáte fecísti: da pópulis tuis spirituálium grátiam gaudiórum; et ómnium fidélium mentes dírige in viam salútis ætérnæ.
content.english: O God, Who hast made this day to be honourable in our eyes because of the Birth of the blessed John, graciously quicken thy people with spiritual joy, and order the minds of all the faithful in the way of everlasting salvation.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Ant. Elísabeth Zacharíæ * magnum virum génuit, Ioánnem Baptístam, præcursórem Dómini.
content.english: Ant. Elizabeth, the wife of Zacharias, * was the mother of a mighty man, even of John the Baptist, the Fore-runner of the Lord.

content.latin: Psalmus 92 [1]
content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Elísabeth Zacharíæ magnum virum génuit, Ioánnem Baptístam, præcursórem Dómini.
content.english: Ant. Elizabeth, the wife of Zacharias, was the mother of a mighty man, even of John the Baptist, the Fore-runner of the Lord.

content.latin: Ant. Innuébant patri eius * quem vellet vocári eum: et scripsit dicens: Ioánnes est nomen eius.
content.english: Ant. They made signs to his father * how he would have him called; and he asked for a writing-table, and wrote, saying: His name is John.

content.latin: Psalmus 99 [2]
content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Innuébant patri eius quem vellet vocári eum: et scripsit dicens: Ioánnes est nomen eius.
content.english: Ant. They made signs to his father how he would have him called; and he asked for a writing-table, and wrote, saying: His name is John.

content.latin: Ant. Ioánnes vocábitur * nomen eius: et in nativitáte eius multi gaudébunt.
content.english: Ant. Thou shalt call his name John; * and many shall rejoice at his birth.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

content.latin: Canticum Trium Puerorum [4]
content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:73 Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.
content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 3:74 Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:75 (Fit reverentia:) Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu: * laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:75 (Bow head) Let us bless the Father and the Son, with the Holy Ghost; * let us praise and exalt him above all for ever.

content.latin: 3:56 Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

content.latin: Ant. Inter natos mulíerum non surréxit maior Ioánne Baptísta.
content.english: Ant. Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.

content.latin: Ant. Tu, puer, * Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis; præíbis ante Dóminum paráre vias eius.
content.english: Ant. Thou, child, shalt be called the Prophet of the Highest; * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord, to prepare His ways.

content.latin: Psalmus 148 [5]
content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

content.latin: Audíte, ínsulæ, et atténdite, pópuli de longe: Dóminus ab útero vocávit me, de ventre matris meæ recordátus est nóminis mei.
content.english: Give ear, ye islands, and hearken, ye people from afar. The Lord hath called me from the womb, from the bowels of my mother he hath been mindful of my name.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

content.latin: O nimis felix, meritíque celsi,
content.english: O more than blessèd, merit high attaining,

content.latin: Nésciens labem nívei pudóris,
content.english: Pure as the snow-drift, innocent of evil,

content.latin: Prǽpotens Martyr, nemorúmque cultor,
content.english: Child of the desert, mightiest of martyrs,

content.latin: Máxime Vatum.
content.english: Greatest of prophets.

content.latin: Serta ter denis álios corónant
content.english: Thirtyfold increase some with glory crowneth;

content.latin: Aucta creméntis, duplicáta quosdam,
content.english: Sixtyfold fruitage prize for others winneth;

content.latin: Trina te fructu cumuláta centum
content.english: Hundredfold measure, thrice repeated, decks thee,

content.latin: Néxibus ornant.
content.english: Blest one, for guerdon.

content.latin: Nunc potens nostri méritis opímis
content.english: O may the virtue of thine intercession,

content.latin: Péctoris duros lápides revélle
content.english: All stony hardness from our hearts expelling,

content.latin: Asperum planans iter, et refléxos
content.english: Smooth the rough places, and the crooked straighten

content.latin: Dírige calles.
content.english: Here in the desert.

content.latin: Ut pius mundi Sator et Redémptor
content.english: Thus may our gracious Maker and Redeemer,

content.latin: Méntibus culpæ sine labe puris
content.english: Seeking a station for his hallowed footsteps,

content.latin: Rite dignétur véniens beátos
content.english: Find, when he cometh, temples undefilèd,

content.latin: Pónere gressus.
content.english: Meet to receive him.

content.latin: Láudibus cives célebrent supérni
content.english: Now as the angels celebrate thy praises,

content.latin: Te, Deus simplex paritérque trine,
content.english: Godhead essential, Trinity co-equal;

content.latin: Súpplices et nos véniam precámur:
content.english: Spare thy redeemed ones, as they bow before thee,

content.latin: Parce redémptis.
content.english: Pardon imploring.

content.english: Amen.

content.english: ℣. The child shall be great in the sight of the Lord.

content.latin: ℟. Nam et manus eius cum ipso est.
content.english: ℟. For His hand is with him.

content.english: Ant. And the mouth of Zacharias was opened, * and he prophesied, saying: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

content.latin: 118:12 Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:12 Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:13 In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
content.english: 118:13 With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.

content.latin: 118:14 In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
content.english: 118:14 I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.

content.latin: 118:15 In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
content.english: 118:15 I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.

content.latin: 118:16 In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:16 I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.

content.latin: 118:20 Concupívit ánima mea desideráre iustificatiónes tuas, * in omni témpore.
content.english: 118:20 My soul hath coveted to long for thy justifications, * at all times.

content.latin: 118:21 Increpásti supérbos: * maledícti qui declínant a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:21 Thou hast rebuked the proud: * they are cursed who decline from thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:22 Aufer a me oppróbrium, et contémptum: * quia testimónia tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:22 Remove from me reproach and contempt: * because I have sought after thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:23 Étenim sedérunt príncipes, et advérsum me loquebántur: * servus autem tuus exercebátur in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:23 For princes sat, and spoke against me: * but thy servant was employed in thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:24 Nam et testimónia tua meditátio mea est: * et consílium meum iustificatiónes tuæ.
content.english: 118:24 For thy testimonies are my meditation: * and thy justifications my counsel.

content.latin: 118:25 (Daleth) Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea: * vivífica me secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:25 (Daleth) My soul hath cleaved to the pavement: * quicken thou me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:26 Vias meas enuntiávi, et exaudísti me: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:26 I have declared my ways, and thou hast heard me: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:27 Viam iustificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me: * et exercébor in mirabílibus tuis.
content.english: 118:27 Make me to understand the way of thy justifications: * and I shall be exercised in thy wondrous works.

content.latin: 118:28 Dormitávit ánima mea præ tǽdio: * confírma me in verbis tuis.

content.latin: 118:30 Viam veritátis elégi: * iudícia tua non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:30 I have chosen the way of truth: * thy judgments I have not forgotten.

content.latin: 118:31 Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis, Dómine: * noli me confúndere.
content.english: 118:31 I have stuck to thy testimonies, O Lord: * put me not to shame.

content.latin: 118:32 Viam mandatórum tuórum cucúrri, * cum dilatásti cor meum.
content.english: 118:32 I have run the way of thy commandments, * when thou didst enlarge my heart.

content.latin: Alexandríæ sancti Gallicáni Mártyris, viri Consuláris, qui, sublimátus ínfulis triumphálibus et Constantíno Augústo carus, a sanctis Ioánne et Paulo ad Christi fidem convérsus est; eáque suscépta, cum sancto Hilaríno secéssit ad Ostia Tiberína, atque ibi hospitalitáti et infirmórum servítio totum se dedit. Cuius rei fama in toto Orbe divulgáta, multi úndique illuc veniéntes vidébant virum ex Patrício et Cónsule laváre páuperum pedes, pónere mensam, aquam mánibus effúndere, languéntibus sollícite ministráre et cétera pietátis offícia exhibére. Ipse póstmodum, sub Iuliáno Apóstata, inde expúlsus, Alexandríam perréxit; ibíque, cum a Rauciáno Iúdice sacrificáre cogerétur et contémneret, ídeo, percússus gládio, Christi Martyr efféctus est.
content.english: At Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Lucy, with twenty-two others.

content.latin: Sibápoli, in Mesopotámia, sanctæ Febróniæ, Vírginis et Mártyris; quæ, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Siléno Iúdice, ob fidem et pudicítiam servándam, primo virgis cæsa et equúleo torta, deínde pectínibus laniáta atque igne succénsa, demum, excússis déntibus ac mammis pedibúsque abscíssis, cápitis damnáta, tot passiónum ornáta monílibus migrávit ad Sponsum.
content.english: At Alexandria, the holy martyr Gallican. This was a man of Consular rank, who had received the honour of a triumph and was a personal friend of the Emperor Constantine. He was converted to the faith of Christ by holy John and Paul. After his conversion he withdrew to Ostia with holy Hilarinus, when he gave himself entirely to the service of strangers and the sick. This got noised abroad in all the world so that people came from all parts to see a man who had been a patrician and a consul washing the feet of the poor, laying the table, pouring water on the guests' hands, ministering carefully to the sick, and performing other offices of mercy. He was turned out of Ostia under the Emperor Julian the Apostate, and went to Alexandria. There the judge Raucian would needs have him sacrifice, and forasmuch as he would not, caused him to be beheaded, and so he became Christ's martyr.

content.latin: Apud Rhégium sancti Prósperi Aquitáni, eiúsdem urbis Epíscopi, eruditióne ac pietáte insígnis, qui advérsus Pelagiános, pro fide cathólica, strénue decertávit.
content.english: At Sibapolis, in Syria, the holy Virgin and martyr Febronia on account of her steadfastness in faith and chastity during the persecution under Diocletian, the judge Lysimachus ordered her to be first beaten with rods and tormented upon the rack, then torn with combs and burnt with fire afterwards her teeth were hammered out and her breasts cut off, and then she was beheaded, and so passed away to her Divine Bridegroom prepared with all these sufferings as a bride adorned for her husband.

content.latin: Tauríni natális sancti Máximi, Epíscopi et Confessóris, doctrína et sanctitáte celebérrimi.
content.english: At Besançon, in Gaul, the holy martyr Antidius, Bishop of Besançon, who for Christ's faith's sake was slain by the Vandals.

content.latin: In Hollándia sancti Adelbérti Confessóris, qui fuit discípulus sancti Willibrórdi Epíscopi.
content.english: At Reggio, holy Prosper of Aquitaine, Bishop of that city, famous for his learning and godliness, who stoutly contended for the Catholic faith against the Pelagians.

content.latin: ℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
content.english: At Turin, the holy Confessor Maximus, Bishop of Turin, very famous for his teaching and holiness.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: In Holland, the holy Confessor Adelbert, the disciple of holy Willibrord, Archbishop [of Utrecht.]
℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:

content.english: ℣. Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.

content.latin: ℟. Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: ℟. And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.english: Benediction. May Almighty God arrange our deeds and our day in His peace.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: 2 Thess 3:5

content.latin: Dóminus autem dírigat corda et córpora nostra in caritáte Dei et patiéntia Christi.
content.english: And the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.english: Ant. They made signs to his father * how he would have him called; and he asked for a writing-table, and wrote, saying: His name is John.

content.latin: 118:33 (He) Legem pone mihi, Dómine, viam iustificatiónum tuárum: * et exquíram eam semper.
content.english: 118:33 (He) Set before me for a law the way of thy justifications, O Lord: * and I will always seek after it.

content.latin: 118:34 Da mihi intelléctum, et scrutábor legem tuam: * et custódiam illam in toto corde meo.
content.english: 118:34 Give me understanding, and I will search thy law; * and I will keep it with my whole heart.

content.latin: 118:35 Deduc me in sémitam mandatórum tuórum: * quia ipsam vólui.
content.english: 118:35 Lead me into the path of thy commandments; * for this same I have desired.

content.latin: 118:36 Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua: * et non in avarítiam.
content.english: 118:36 Incline my heart into thy testimonies * and not to covetousness.

content.latin: 118:37 Avérte óculos meos ne vídeant vanitátem: * in via tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:37 Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity: * quicken me in thy way.

content.latin: 118:38 Státue servo tuo elóquium tuum, * in timóre tuo.
content.english: 118:38 Establish thy word to thy servant, * in thy fear.

content.latin: 118:39 Ámputa oppróbrium meum quod suspicátus sum: * quia iudícia tua iucúnda.
content.english: 118:39 Turn away my reproach, which I have apprehended: * for thy judgments are delightful.

content.latin: 118:40 Ecce, concupívi mandáta tua: * in æquitáte tua vivífica me.
content.english: 118:40 Behold I have longed after thy precepts: * quicken me in thy justice.

content.latin: 118:41 (Vav) Et véniat super me misericórdia tua, Dómine: * salutáre tuum secúndum elóquium tuum.
content.english: 118:41 (Vau) Let thy mercy also come upon me, O Lord: * thy salvation according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:42 Et respondébo exprobrántibus mihi verbum: * quia sperávi in sermónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:42 So shall I answer them that reproach me in any thing; * that I have trusted in thy words.

content.latin: 118:43 Et ne áuferas de ore meo verbum veritátis usquequáque: * quia in iudíciis tuis supersperávi.
content.english: 118:43 And take not thou the word of truth utterly out of my mouth: * for in thy words, I have hoped exceedingly.

content.latin: 118:44 Et custódiam legem tuam semper: * in sǽculum et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 118:44 So shall I always keep thy law, * for ever and ever.

content.latin: 118:45 Et ambulábam in latitúdine: * quia mandáta tua exquisívi.
content.english: 118:45 And I walked at large: * because I have sought after thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:46 Et loquébar in testimóniis tuis in conspéctu regum: * et non confundébar.
content.english: 118:46 And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings: * and I was not ashamed.

content.latin: 118:47 Et meditábar in mandátis tuis, * quæ diléxi.
content.english: 118:47 I meditated also on thy commandments, * which I loved.

content.latin: 118:48 Et levávi manus meas ad mandáta tua, quæ diléxi: * et exercébar in iustificatiónibus tuis.
content.english: 118:48 And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments, which I loved: * and I was exercised in thy justifications.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:49 (Zai) Memor esto verbi tui servo tuo, * in quo mihi spem dedísti.
content.english: 118:49 (Zai) Be thou mindful of thy word to thy servant, * in which thou hast given me hope.

content.latin: 118:50 Hæc me consoláta est in humilitáte mea: * quia elóquium tuum vivificávit me.
content.english: 118:50 This hath comforted me in my humiliation: * because thy word hath enlivened me.

content.latin: 118:51 Supérbi iníque agébant usquequáque: * a lege autem tua non declinávi.
content.english: 118:51 The proud did iniquitously altogether: * but I declined not from thy law.

content.latin: 118:52 Memor fui iudiciórum tuórum a sǽculo, Dómine: * et consolátus sum.
content.english: 118:52 I remembered, O Lord, thy judgments of old: * and I was comforted.

content.latin: 118:53 Deféctio ténuit me, * pro peccatóribus derelinquéntibus legem tuam.
content.english: 118:53 A fainting hath taken hold of me, * because of the wicked that forsake thy law.

content.latin: 118:54 Cantábiles mihi erant iustificatiónes tuæ, * in loco peregrinatiónis meæ.
content.english: 118:54 Thy justifications were the subject of my song, * in the place of my pilgrimage.

content.latin: 118:55 Memor fui nocte nóminis tui, Dómine: * et custodívi legem tuam.
content.english: 118:55 In the night I have remembered thy name, O Lord: * and have kept thy law.

content.latin: 118:56 Hæc facta est mihi: * quia iustificatiónes tuas exquisívi.
content.english: 118:56 This happened to me: * because I sought after thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:57 (Heth) Pórtio mea, Dómine, * dixi custodíre legem tuam.
content.english: 118:57 (Heth) O Lord, my portion, * I have said, I would keep thy law.

content.latin: 118:58 Deprecátus sum fáciem tuam in toto corde meo: * miserére mei secúndum elóquium tuum.
content.english: 118:58 I entreated thy face with all my heart: * have mercy on me according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:59 Cogitávi vias meas: * et convérti pedes meos in testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:59 I have thought on my ways: * and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:60 Parátus sum, et non sum turbátus: * ut custódiam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:60 I am ready, and am not troubled: * that I may keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:61 Funes peccatórum circumpléxi sunt me: * et legem tuam non sum oblítus.
content.english: 118:61 The cords of the wicked have encompassed me: * but I have not forgotten thy law.

content.latin: 118:62 Média nocte surgébam ad confiténdum tibi, * super iudícia iustificatiónis tuæ.
content.english: 118:62 I rose at midnight to give praise to thee; * for the judgments of thy justification.

content.latin: 118:63 Párticeps ego sum ómnium timéntium te: * et custodiéntium mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:63 I am a partaker with all them that fear thee, * and that keep thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:64 Misericórdia tua, Dómine, plena est terra: * iustificatiónes tuas doce me.
content.english: 118:64 The earth, O Lord, is full of thy mercy: * teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 118:65 (Teth) Bonitátem fecísti cum servo tuo, Dómine, * secúndum verbum tuum.
content.english: 118:65 (Teth) Thou hast done well with thy servant, O Lord, * according to thy word.

content.latin: 118:66 Bonitátem, et disciplínam, et sciéntiam doce me: * quia mandátis tuis crédidi.
content.english: 118:66 Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge; * for I have believed thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:67 Priúsquam humiliárer ego delíqui: * proptérea elóquium tuum custodívi.
content.english: 118:67 Before I was humbled I offended; * therefore have I kept thy word.

content.latin: 118:68 Bonus es tu: * et in bonitáte tua doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:68 Thou art good; * and in thy goodness teach me thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:69 Multiplicáta est super me iníquitas superbórum: * ego autem in toto corde meo scrutábor mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:69 The iniquity of the proud hath been multiplied over me: * but I will seek thy commandments with my whole heart.

content.latin: 118:70 Coagulátum est sicut lac cor eórum: * ego vero legem tuam meditátus sum.
content.english: 118:70 Their heart is curdled like milk: * but I have meditated on thy law.

content.latin: 118:71 Bonum mihi quia humiliásti me: * ut discam iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:71 It is good for me that thou hast humbled me, * that I may learn thy justifications.

content.latin: 118:72 Bonum mihi lex oris tui, * super míllia auri et argénti.
content.english: 118:72 The law of thy mouth is good to me, * above thousands of gold and silver.

content.latin: 118:73 (Ioth) Manus tuæ fecérunt me, et plasmavérunt me: * da mihi intelléctum, et discam mandáta tua.
content.english: 118:73 (Jod) Thy hands have made me and formed me: * give me understanding, and I will learn thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:74 Qui timent te vidébunt me, et lætabúntur: * quia in verba tua supersperávi.
content.english: 118:74 They that fear thee shall see me, and shall be glad: * because I have greatly hoped in thy words.

content.latin: 118:75 Cognóvi, Dómine, quia ǽquitas iudícia tua: * et in veritáte tua humiliásti me.
content.english: 118:75 I know, O Lord, that thy judgments are equity: * and in thy truth thou hast humbled me.

content.latin: 118:76 Fiat misericórdia tua ut consolétur me, * secúndum elóquium tuum servo tuo.
content.english: 118:76 O! let thy mercy be for my comfort, * according to thy word unto thy servant.

content.latin: 118:77 Véniant mihi miseratiónes tuæ, et vivam: * quia lex tua meditátio mea est.
content.english: 118:77 Let thy tender mercies come unto me, and I shall live: * for thy law is my meditation.

content.latin: 118:78 Confundántur supérbi, quia iniúste iniquitátem fecérunt in me: * ego autem exercébor in mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:78 Let the proud be ashamed, because they have done unjustly towards me: * but I will be employed in thy commandments.

content.latin: 118:79 Convertántur mihi timéntes te: * et qui novérunt testimónia tua.
content.english: 118:79 Let them that fear thee turn to me: * and they that know thy testimonies.

content.latin: 118:80 Fiat cor meum immaculátum in iustificatiónibus tuis, * ut non confúndar.
content.english: 118:80 Let my heart be undefiled in thy justifications, * that I may not be confounded.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
